limitations: Wire runs host clients and all ten service instances in one process; their ten or 100 drives share one Partition. SDK runs invoke stores directly. This is not ten independent deployed service processes.

Retained diagnostic TiDB/PD/TiKV cluster counters include background traffic. Datastore capture windows are broader than workload windows, so normalized backend costs are observed fixture amplification rather than exclusive request attribution.

VM cgroup and proc counters do not measure physical Mac SSD operations, flash writes, or production capacity; no host block device was selected. RustFS physical/backend I/O is not captured by these TiDB observer metrics.

System Rust allocation totals cover the whole clients/server pipeline and background; foreign C allocators, including SQLite heap activity, are excluded. Atomic allocator instrumentation affects throughput. Nonzero values cannot support zero-allocation claims.
Direct SDK storage instrumentation is available. Production remote client, service diagnostics observer, OIDC validation, peer cache, and NAPI forwarding-box sites are unavailable or not configured.
Zero storage-profile SQL byte fields do not establish zero metadata payload. Metadata return and serialization bytes here come from core named provider counters.

Method and stage wall durations are inclusive, nested and parallel, and must not be summed as exclusive CPU time. Endpoint gauges and relaxed snapshots do not prove all provider/background work quiesced.

All qualified wire arms have zero logical failures, zero counter resets, complete metric series, and successful stored/fresh file verification. Durability settings are not crash or power-loss validation.

The ten-client wire comparison has two samples per variant; per-run throughput and latency bounds vary. No statistical confidence interval, exact query-plan cause, capacity, or large-namespace scaling claim follows from this small namespace result.
Single run per arm at each file count; no statistical confidence interval.
Cache occupancy and admission gauges are available, while cache hit/miss counts and all-file warmness are unavailable. No peer cache is configured.
Process allocations cover the full measured SDK pipeline and background, exclude foreign C allocators, and profiling atomics affect throughput.
Named SQL counts and HTTP connector attempts are method accounting, not physical SSD IOPS. SQL byte fields are unavailable; core provider counters give known returned/serialized bytes.
Successful whole-file byte, EOF, exact root membership and cleanup checks do not test crash durability.

Compact root-file capability is initialized outside the timed windows. The SDK records read_compact_root_entry under the shared load_compact_root_file label: timed calls are ordinary root-entry lookups, not complete root-file snapshot reads. Timed root-file-capability calls are zero.

method.SDK: two drives and five independent filesystem/pool clients per drive; 100 or 1000 files/drive; 100 iterations/lane/pattern; 1000 cycles/pattern; cycle includes Open, one 4KiB Read plus byte/EOF checks or Overwrite, and Close; SDK cycles are not preopened wire IOPS; default SDK cache, hit/miss counts unavailable, no peer cache
method.allocations: whole measured process pipeline and background, System Rust allocator only; foreign C allocators excluded; profiling atomics affect throughput
method.backend: TiDB/PD/TiKV counters include cluster/background work and capture windows broader than workload; Linux VM cgroup/proc I/O is not physical Mac SSD I/O; RustFS physical I/O not covered
method.datastore: retained diagnostic TiDB v8.5.7: one TiDB, three PD, three TiKV; loopback RustFS 1.0.0 with durable blocks and persistent bind mount; Docker VM 14 CPUs and 16745295872 bytes memory; not production capacity or crash durability validation
method.selected_SQL_definition: inode_read + inode_write + metadata_read + metadata_write; session and transaction method calls reported separately; these counts differ from TiDB process statement counters
method.wire: 4KiB binary v2 reads/writes on preopened handles; one process, ten service instances, one Partition, separate Drive per active client; depth one/client; 32 hot blocks/file; warm SDK/catalog caches, no peer cache; synthetic authentication, request audit included; release with allocation/resource profiling and 16 Tokio workers
method.wire_10: ten active clients and ten drives; two runs/variant in baseline-current-current-baseline order; IOPS = sum(completed)/sum(elapsed including drain); resource costs weighted by successes; p95 values are ranges of per-run power-of-two microsecond histogram upper bounds
method.wire_100: 100 active clients, 100 drives, ten service instances, one process and one Partition; one measured run per variant; maximum measured client count is 100, with no production 10000-client qualification

qualification_notes.baseline_a: Original supervisor required inline test ok; child observer prints between test prefix and bare ok. Exact one named case plus running1 plus bareok plus final1pass validated without replay.

measured_SDK_harness.later_cleanup_hardening: Streams bounded inventories across all owned scopes before any mutation. This post-measurement cleanup change does not change workload, setup, oracle or metrics code; no measurement replay.

qualification_notes.raw_artifacts: Private raw artifacts and inventories are not committed. Content hashes bind the derived report to qualified inputs. No raw connection config, endpoints or credentials are included.

reproduction.build: release, locked, allocation-profiling (enables resource/io profiling), jobs=1, distinct CARGO_TARGET_DIR per checkout
reproduction.harness: Use identical harness bytes in both checkouts. Original measured harness hash is retained; later cleanup-only source changes do not alter old binary qualification.
reproduction.timing: Build first; run emitted executable directly and serially; no Cargo/build activity during timing
